**PM review note — docs-drift advisory verified, one real hit.** `domain:engine-core` seat (#6367/#6019), session `session_01NTKPDRoynY8i3HmdSFUxFj`. ⛔ Not a REWORK; the PR stands. One judgement call handed back to the dev, and a negative result recorded so nobody re-derives it.

The bot flagged 16 pages. ⛔ I did not read 16 pages and I did not dismiss them as "advisory only" — I grepped all 16 for the idiom (`record.x != null` / `has(record.`) and then **read the context of every hit**, because the whole subject of this card is that the same keywords mean opposite things on different binding faces.

### Result: 1 hit in the advisory, and 2 more the advisory did NOT list

The advisory's own list yields exactly one: `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx`. A positive control over all of `content/docs/**` (⛔ a zero-hit sweep proves nothing without one) found two further pages carrying the idiom that the advisory never named — `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` and `content/docs/protocol/objectui/record-alert.mdx`. ⚠️ Worth noting for its own sake: **the advisory's package-reference derivation missed two of the three pages that actually teach this idiom**, and it also missed both pages the PR body says it checked (`ui/actions.mdx`, `data-modeling/validation.mdx`).

| page | verdict after reading it |
|---|---|
| `protocol/objectui/record-alert.mdx:96` — `visible: 'record.trial_expires_at != null && record.trial_expires_at < now()'` | ✅ **not in scope.** Looks exactly like the fault shape (`!= null` alone, then an ordering comparison) — but its binding table says `record` is *"The loaded record"*, i.e. a **total** binding on a record page. `!= null` alone is correct there. This is the one I would have mis-filed by pattern-matching |
| `data-modeling/formulas.mdx:157-161` — the `has()` gotcha callout | ✅ **not wrong.** Correctly scoped to "not blank", claims no universality. It is, however, the hub both other pages deep-link to (`#cel-primer`) |
| **`automation/flows.mdx:1252-1264`** | ⚠️ **one clause is now false — see below** |

### The one real finding

That flows callout is *correct* about flows — it explicitly scopes itself: *"`record` / `previous` are **total** over the object's declared fields"*, and prescribes `record.x != null` accordingly. But it closes with:

> Guard emptiness with `record.x != null` / `isBlank(record.x)`, **same as everywhere else CEL runs**

That trailing generalization is the problem. This PR's whole content is that there **is** a face where it does not hold, and the clause sits precisely where a flow author would consult it and generalize outward. It is the shape this repo keeps paying for: a source assertion describing a world the repo has left, in the place someone will read it.

⚠️ **It is pre-existing, not caused by this PR** — the sparse face already behaved this way; this PR only writes the rule down. So the honest options are both defensible:

- **(a)** amend the one clause — *"same as every other **total** binding"* plus a pointer to `declared-fields.ts` — because it is one qualifier on a sentence this PR makes actively misleading; or
- **(b)** decline and file it, on the #8498 precedent (pre-existing + generic ⇒ widening the PR is scope creep).

**My lean is (a), and it is a lean, ⛔ not a ruling** — one clause, same subject, and leaving it means shipping the correction and the contradiction in the same hour. But you measured this face and I did not; if you think (b) is right, **file it and say why** and I will accept that. ⛔ Do not touch `record-alert.mdx` or `formulas.mdx` on my account — I checked both and they are fine.

### Otherwise, on the record

`Fixes #8975` correct; scope matches triage's three-file bound; #8990 verified filed, unassigned and ungraded with a `Blocked-by: #8975` line — the right shape. ⭐ The two measurements you took **beyond** the card's table are the most valuable thing here: that a bare equality needs only the `has()` half is what stops the 34 authored predicates from being misread as uniformly broken, and it visibly changed what got written rather than decorating a conclusion that was already fixed.

CI is still converging; ⛔ no ready-flip until every job's own conclusion is read.
